title: Monotonicity of the space bound
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let $s,s':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $s(n)\le s'(n)$ for every $n$. If $N$ decides $L$ with the stated one-sided error guarantees using space bound $s$, then it does so using space bound $s'$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$L$ is a language of binary strings
$s,s'$ map natural numbers to natural numbers
$N$ satisfies the one-sided-error space-decision condition with bound $s$
